title: Baked Timelines, Lanes, Shrinkwrap, Fields & a Morphing Toast
description: A solved arcade round written as pure CSS keyframes, WebKit's grid-lanes, canvas-measured shrinkwrap, proximity as a CSS variable, and a toast that morphs.

drops.title: The Game Is Baked Into the Keyframes
drops.description: A deterministic solver plays the whole invasion up front, then writes every event out as a CSS keyframe stop.
drops.concept: Commit Invaders simulates a full Space Invaders round against your contribution graph offline, then maps each simulation event to a percentage in a CSS @keyframes timeline so the SVG plays with no JavaScript at all — which is what makes it safe inside a GitHub README. This drop rebuilds that pipeline: cells are plucked from the grid, hatch into sprites drawn in box-shadow pixels, march, and are shot down, with the whole choreography emitted once into a <style> tag and nothing running afterwards.

interaction.mouse: Drag the fleet, loop and grid-density sliders to re-solve the timeline
interaction.click: Re-solve rolls a new seed and writes a fresh set of keyframes
interaction.touch: Everything plays itself — the controls are the only input

drops.title: Lanes, Not Columns
drops.description: display: grid-lanes places each item in the lane that leaves it closest to the top — a waterfall from columns, bricks from rows.
drops.concept: Grid Lanes landed in Safari Technology Preview as a new layout mode: lanes are declared with ordinary grid-template-* properties, orientation is inferred from which one you set, and fit-tolerance controls how big a height difference has to be before the algorithm jumps lanes. The demo runs natively where the browser supports it and falls back to a shim that applies exactly the same placement rule, with lane tints and a shuffle to watch the decision change.
drops.source: WebKit Blog — Introducing CSS Grid Lanes

interaction.mouse: Change lane count, gap and fit-tolerance and watch items re-place
interaction.click: Waterfall/Brick flips orientation; shuffle reorders the source list
interaction.touch: Controls stack under the gallery on narrow screens

drops.title: Type That Knows Its Own Width
drops.description: Measure the text in canvas, find the widest wrapped line, and the bubble shrinks to exactly that.
drops.concept: Pretext measures multiline text without touching the DOM — prepare() caches every segment's width via canvas, layout() is arithmetic over those numbers — which unlocks the multiline shrink-wrap CSS has never had. This drop runs that pipeline on a chat thread: toggle between CSS max-width and measured shrinkwrap, see the dead space hatched in, and compare the measured width against what the browser actually rendered.

interaction.mouse: Max width, font size and letter spacing re-run prepare/layout live
interaction.click: Switch measurement mode; line boxes draw each measured line's width
interaction.touch: Panel drops below the thread on phones

drops.title: Proximity Is a CSS Variable
drops.description: One pointer listener publishes --nf and a unit vector, and magnetic, tilt and glow fall out of calc().
drops.concept: Near-field replaces binary hover with a continuous value: distance from the element's nearest edge, eased over a radius, handed to CSS as --nf plus --nf-x / --nf-y. A single passive pointermove and one shared rAF loop feed every subscriber, with springs integrated at a fixed 120Hz substep so the feel doesn't change with refresh rate. Nine elements here read the same three properties.

interaction.mouse: Move near the buttons, cards and panel — nothing needs to be hovered
interaction.click: Feel presets and the radius/stiffness/damping sliders retune the field
interaction.touch: Touch has no 'near', so a press supplies the value instead

drops.title: One Toast That Morphs in Place
drops.description: The toast on screen springs to the next size while its text swaps, instead of a new one stacking under it.
drops.concept: Ding animates a toast's size and shape on a spring solver rather than fixed-duration easing, and reuses the toast already on screen so loading -> success is one object changing its mind. Held toasts — errors, anything with a button — stay put, and the held mode decides whether quick toasts sit beside them, queue behind them, or replace them. Interrupting a morph keeps its momentum, which the counter here tracks.

interaction.mouse: Fire each toast variant and watch the same element resize
interaction.click: Undo returns a patch that morphs the toast; held modes change the rules
interaction.touch: All buttons are tap targets; the stage is full width on phones
